| [QUESTION-190](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-190.md) | Is the ε⁻² sample complexity of estimating the bisimulation metric between finite Markov chains from occupancy samples optimal, and does an estimator keep a polynomial guarantee on samples from one running trajectory? | Filed when the promotion audit (batch 042, [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2) narrowed and promoted [THEORY-280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-280.md). Theorem 1 of Calo et al. ([LIT-948](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-948.md)) was re-checked: an ε-accurate estimate from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|)log(1/δ))/((1−γ)²ε²)) independent occupancy samples per chain. That the ε⁻² rate is optimal was part of the former promote_when, and this question holds it, with the single-stream case the authors expect but do not test. | Open |
| [QUESTION-195](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-195.md) | Does prior-scored translation without parallel data keep an error bound that falls in the common ground and the size of the source language when the languages are not uniform or the translators are lossy? | Filed when the promotion audit (batch 044, [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2) narrowed and promoted THEORY-270 to Goldwasser and co-authors' common-nonsense theorem, re-derived from its appendix. The former promote_when, a bound outside the uniform, lossless models, is held here. | Open |
| [QUESTION-200](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-200.md) | Is the subspace-patching effect measured in GPT-2 Small's layer-8 MLP an instance of the dormant-direction construction, rather than two cancelling subspaces in that component, and does its dependence on the disconnected component replicate in a second model family? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md). [THEORY-282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md) was promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2) for what its construction proves: a subspace patch can reproduce a variable's output effect without localizing it. Whether the measured cases are such patches, rather than two cancelling subspaces in the patched component, is open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-209](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-209.md) | Do listeners in reference and signalling games invert an informative speaker when alternatives and costs are manipulated with the uttered form held fixed, the model's parameters are set in advance, and its predictions are tested on trial-level data against a literal listener and a likelihood-only model? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md). [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) was promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3) on what was measured: in Frank and Goodman's reference games listeners' mean bets matched a parameter-free inverted informative speaker with a measured salience prior, and in Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling games listeners read a novel signal by its alternative. The evidence is a fit of condition means with no rival model fitted. | Open |
| [QUESTION-210](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-210.md) | Does the QQ equality of survey question-order data hold in question pairs chosen in advance by investigators other than its proposers, and does a classical model with memory, constrained to satisfy it, fit the per-pair tables as well as the projection model? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md). [THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md) was promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3) on what Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin and Busemeyer measured: across the 66 Pew surveys of 2001-2011 that varied the order of two back-to-back questions, order changed the answers but not the probability of agreeing answers. The pairs were chosen by the equality's proposers' team from one organisation's archive, and no constrained classical rival was fitted. | Open |
| [QUESTION-211](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-211.md) | How far are independently trained latent spaces from a cosine-preserving map: is the held-out residual of the best orthogonal-times-scalar map close to that of the best linear map where anchor-based stitching works, and does the gap grow where it fails? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md). [THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md) was promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3) on its invariance, re-derived, and on what Moschella et al. measured: independently trained encoders agree in their cosine profiles to matched anchors only approximately, enough for untrained decoder transfer with loss, while their nearest neighbours mostly differ. The source never fits a map between two spaces. | Open |
| [QUESTION-214](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-214.md) | Do colour-naming systems stay near the information-bottleneck bound when the need distribution is measured independently of the naming data, and do lexicons in a second semantic domain? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md) was narrowed to what Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier and Tishby measured and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3): the World Color Survey languages and English lie near the information-bottleneck curve at a trade-off parameter just above 1, nearer than hue-rotated variants of themselves, with a need distribution estimated from the naming data. A test with an independently measured source, or in a second domain, is open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-216](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-216.md) | Does the output Fisher–Rao geometry agreement across language models replicate with released code, and does it fall when models are fitted to different laws while their activation geometry stays as it was, with only a small part of the shared eigenvector structure exceeding a fair law-matched null? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md). [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md) was narrowed and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2 and v3). Its identification is re-derived: the Fisher–Rao geometry of next-token laws is a function of the laws. Its measurement is one study read in full: mean rank agreement 0.88 against 0.62 in Picozzi's ten models, and about 9% of the top eigenvector overlap beyond a displacement-matched null. Replication, and a test that varies the law, are open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-226](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-226.md) | Does Pearl's Causality define intervention as surgery on autonomous equations throughout, in the chapters on identification and the do-calculus, on structural counterfactuals, and on whether do(x) is universal, and what conditions does it put on the surgery there? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-419](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-419.md). [THEORY-419](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-419.md) was narrowed to the do-operator as Pearl defines it in the pages of Causality that [NOTE-696](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-696.md) read, and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2). Whether the book defines intervention the same way in the chapters not read is open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-240](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-240.md) | Does a transport whose local kernels commute with restriction preserve overlap consistency, and does a transport induced by one global stochastic kernel preserve global extendability? | The part of [QUESTION-022](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-022.md) the manuscript's Propositions 1 and 2 settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). Yes to both, for finite scenarios: [CLAIM-121](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-121.md) for overlap consistency and [CLAIM-070](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-070.md) for global extendability. Both are sufficient conditions. Whether they are necessary, and what transports that change the cover do, stays with [QUESTION-022](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-022.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-245](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-245.md) | For linear decisions at the population level, if a kind's admissible transformations are given as a distribution over pairs of its realizations, is the top eigenspace of the pair operator a stable, decision-sufficient span, and what span takes that role when the pairs are directed? | The linear part of [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). For symmetric pairs, yes: the top eigenfunctions are the most view-invariant directions, and their span is minimax-optimal for linear prediction of approximately view-invariant targets ([THEORY-007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md)) and bounds linear-probe error by leakage over conductance ([THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md)). For directed pairs, the top left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator take that role ([THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md)), and a linear readout of the full density ratio suffices for redundant labels ([THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md)). Other spans can tie. Nonlinear decisions, and what picks one signature out, stay with [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-246](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-246.md) | In quantum theory, what does a failure of Kochen–Specker noncontextuality refute, as against a failure of Spekkens's generalized noncontextuality, and which of the two notions is broader? | The conceptual part of [QUESTION-067](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-067.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md), [THEORY-015](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md), [THEORY-016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md), [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) and [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md). A Kochen–Specker proof refutes measurement noncontextuality together with outcome determinism, and so universal generalized noncontextuality. A generalized no-go refutes a positive quasiprobability representation, and Leibnizian representations within classical realism. The generalized notion is strictly broader. Which notion a test of pragmatic judgements can reach stays with [QUESTION-067](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-067.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-247](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-247.md) v2 | If the communicative object is a presheaf of propositions over a category of contexts, is the negation its topos logic gives an orthocomplement or a Heyting pseudo-complement, and what fixes it? | The conditional part of [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) and [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md). Over a presheaf of contexts the truth values are sieves, and negation is the Heyting pseudo-complement that the base category fixes, not an orthocomplement. That the communicative object is such a presheaf is QUESTION-332, Answered by CLAIM-038. Over which base, and whether probes split it into sectors, stays with [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-249](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-249.md) | If a map of a representation X of finite support keeps no information about a categorical concept A, how much information about X can it keep, and when does it keep that much? | The one-step, information-theoretic part of [QUESTION-010](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-010.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md). The map can keep at most H(X\|A), and it keeps that much exactly when X is a function of the output and A. A deterministic map gets there only when the concept groups' distributions are permutations of one another. Chains, and relations as against a categorical label, stay with [QUESTION-010](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-010.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-272](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-272.md) v2 | When the task's target and the probes' outcome laws are both linear in one unknown state, as for the pairwise comparisons of actions under partial monitoring and for the authority shares of a mixture of known response profiles, when does a family of probes separate what the task needs told apart? | The part of [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) that the readings of 2026-10-25 settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). Both answers are linear: a probe family separates what the task needs exactly when the task's target lies in the span of what the probes reveal. For pairwise comparisons of actions under partial monitoring, that is the loss difference lying in the probes' combined signal row space ([THEORY-962](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md)). For the authority shares of a mixture of known profiles, it is the profiles over the probe contexts being affinely independent ([CLAIM-452](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-452.md)). The general stochastic, decision-relative case, where the target or the outcome laws are not linear in a common state, stays with [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-293](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-293.md) | Is the distortion of a composite of approximate transports bounded by the sum of its parts' distortions, and does that additive bound survive when the distortion lacks a triangle inequality or a later kernel stretches distances? | The additive part of [QUESTION-017](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-017.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-260](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-260.md) (Active) settles it in full. The composite of an ε₁-transport and an ε₂-transport is an (Lε₁ + ε₂)-transport when the distortion obeys a triangle inequality, with L the later kernel's stretch, so additive when that kernel is nonexpansive, as every Markov kernel is in total variation. Without a triangle inequality, or with an expansive kernel, the additive bound fails. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-296](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-296.md) | Can an intervention on what an interpreter is told about a communicative situation tell the relations that constitute the act from those that only accompany it? | The part of [QUESTION-030](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-030.md)'s empirical half that [CLAIM-130](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-130.md) settles, split off by the status review of 2026-10-28 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). No: telling an interpreter about the situation, do(I), acts on a different variable from changing the situation, do(S). Its effect is evidence about interpretation under instruction, and bears on constitution only through a do(S). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-321](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-321.md) | For finitely many states, does "at least as informative in every bounded decision problem" imply simulation by a Markov kernel when the simulated experiment's outcome space is not standard Borel? | The part of the promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) that the twelfth status review's re-derivation does not reach. Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), claims the equivalence for arbitrary outcome spaces through its Theorem 2, quoted from Blackwell (1951), which the record has not read. The record's proof needs a regular conditional distribution of the simulated experiment's outcome given its posterior, so [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) was narrowed to standard Borel spaces and promoted. | Open |
| [QUESTION-323](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-323.md) | After an anchoring comparison, is anchor-consistent knowledge more accessible on a measure first shown sensitive to direct priming, and does the difference go with the size of the estimate shift? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-335](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md), moved here when the twelfth status review promoted it on a title that claims only the moderations and the failed test, as [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md)'s moved to [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md). Whether the accessibility step is real is this question. | Open |
| [QUESTION-332](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-332.md) | Is the communicative object a presheaf over contexts? | The first remaining part of [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), split off by the fourteenth status review under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) because [CLAIM-038](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-038.md) (Active since 2026-10-29) settles it: a communicative object is a context-indexed system of empirical constraints over a cover of contexts, supports or distributions with their restrictions ([TERM-042](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-042.md)), which is a presheaf over contexts. Which base category it has, and whether some probe family splits it into sectors, stays [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md)'s. | Answered |
